claims.text: Anyone can enter chat.culture.dev with just their email: they type it, a code lands in their inbox, and they're in the sandbox as a guest -- no password, no account setup

An email-only visitor (not in auth.allowed_emails, no password) reaches a code mail without needing to discover the 'Guest mode' secondary button: today POST /entry/email always renders the password window (entry.py post_email) and the only email-only path is the outline 'Guest mode' button beside 'Sign in' (entry.html.j2:59)

hard_questions.text: Which UX shape? (A) step 1 offers 'Continue with email only' that skips the password window and goes straight to nickname+consent+code; (B) keep one flow, and Sign in with an UNKNOWN email mails a guest code to that mailbox (browser answer unchanged, so c3 holds) with nickname/consent collected after the code; (C) keep the flow, just promote 'Guest mode' (primary button / copy saying 'no password? use Guest mode')
hard_questions.resolution: B (user, 2026-10-26): Sign in is the only entry. An email that is not an approved (signed) user gets a guest code mailed on Sign in; the code screen and the code itself look the same for both tiers. The Guest mode button goes away.

claims.text: Approved-user sign-in stays oracle-free: the page, status, timing floor and lens_signin cookie for /entry/signin must stay identical for approved vs unknown emails (entry.py _post_signin_app docstring, obligation o4). Only the mailbox may learn anything

The existing guest pipeline (POST /entry/guest -> /entry/guest/start -> /entry/verify, guest_store tokens, lens_guest cookie, sbx-* nick, consent v1.1) is the 'anonymous account'; the feature reuses it rather than inventing a new account tier

Gmail plus-aliases (you+test@gmail.com) work end-to-end as distinct guests: _norm_email only strips+lowercases (keeps '+'), _plausible_email accepts it, and guest_store keys guests/tokens/consent by the full normalized address -- so a +test alias is a clean test identity separate from the owner's approved address

One guest at a time stays (config guest_mode.max_guests: 1, ~/.config/irc-lens/config.yaml:45); an email-only visitor arriving while the seat is taken gets the busy page and no code (entry.py post_guest_start c24 check) -- the feature does not raise capacity
Set-or-reset-password (/password) stays approved-only: setpw.py post_password mails a link only when email is in allowed_lower(config); email-only visitors get no password and no account upgrade

The code mail goes out at most one screen after the visitor gives their email. Today the guest route is email -> password window -> Guest mode -> nickname + two checkboxes + Enter, and only that last submit (POST /entry/guest/start) sends mail; a visitor who stops at any earlier screen, or whose Enter is blocked by browser validation (nickname pattern [A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,16}, required consent box), gets nothing and sees no explanation
Sign in only: one entry flow. If the email is not a signed (approved) user, Sign in mails a guest code; the code screen and the key look the same for both

The visitor must not be able to tell whether they are a guest or a signed user until after they pass the emailed code: every screen, status and timing up to and including the code screen is the same for both
Consent is a one-time form shown after the emailed code is accepted, and only to a guest who hasn't consented yet; a returning guest who already consented goes straight in

Nickname is collected on that same one-time post-code form (today it's asked before the code on /entry/guest), and the existing consents row (record_consent against current legal versions) is what makes it one-time. If the Terms/Privacy version changes, the guest is asked once more

A guest has no password: their credential is the code mailed to them. Whatever they type in the Password field (or nothing) is ignored for a non-approved email; Sign in mails the code and the guest types it into the Code field on the next screen, the same screen an approved user sees

revisions.text: For a guest the password field is ignored: anything or nothing typed still mails a guest code, because the emailed code is the guest's credential
revisions.reason: user 2026-10-26: 'the credential is the email they sent'

claims.text: A guest can log out: ends their sandbox session, frees the guest seat and clears the lens_guest cookie (today POST /logout is approved-only and a closed tab holds the seat until the 15-min idle reaper)

Guest credential is a single-use code: every Sign in by a non-approved email mails a fresh one-time code, typed on the same code screen approved users see; returning guests get a new code each time (no reusable guest password)

Found a shared-IP lockout the unit tests missed: guest sign-ins counted as wrong passwords against the per-IP limit (3/15 min), so 2 guest sign-ins + 1 wrong approved password from one IP silently blocked the approved user's right password. Fixed: guest submissions are refunded like correct passwords; guest mail is capped by rate_limits.entry_per_min per email and IP instead. Re-run after the fix: guests g1/g2 mailed, approved wrong pw mailed nothing, approved right pw mailed a sign-in code and reached the mesh
